newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Fed, SEC oppose plan for financial council.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Fed, SEC oppose plan for financial council.

text.p: Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan and Securities and Exchange Commission Arthur Levitt voiced opposition Thursday to a Congressional proposal to create a National Council on Financial Services.
Levitt described the proposal, which is contained in a financial reform bill passed by the House Banking Committee, as a "thoroughly rotten idea."

Greenspan was more reserved, although he also made clear his opposition to the creation of a new regulatory council on top of the existing web of financial supervisors. "If it ain't broke, don't fix it," he told a House Commerce subcommittee.

The new council, which would be composed of a variety of bank, securities and insurance regulators, would be designed to help implement the wide-ranging reforms of the financial system that are proposed in the Banking Committee bill.
